title: perf(canary): adaptive KV hysteresis + sensitivity tuning for performance canary auto-detection and rollout guards
author: Asha Gupta
description:
Context: Our continuous performance canary service detects latency/throughput regressions and gates automated rollouts. We observed two classes of flapping regressions: short-lived KV cache pressure spikes that self-resolve and longer regressions caused by model/kernel changes. Motivation: reduce false positives (spurious rollbacks) while keeping sensitivity to real regressions. This PR introduces an adaptive hysteresis detector for KV-related latency signals, per-model sensitivity tuning, and additional rollout guard checks before automated traffic shifts.

What this changes: Checklist:
- [x] Implement adaptive hysteresis state machine in perf/canary/detector.go
- [x] Add per-model sensitivity profiles and config overrides (config map + helm values)
- [x] Capture new metrics and expose gating metrics for Redwood Console (canary.hysteresis_state, canary.sensitivity_profile)
- [x] Add integration tests that simulate transient KV pressure and sustained regressions
- [x] Update docs: docs/perf-canary.md with tuning guidance and failure modes

Design highlights: The detector tracks short-window and long-window latency percentiles separately and applies a hysteresis controller whose thresholds adapt based on recent KV miss-rate and sequence-length distribution. The goal is to require a sustained degradation across both windows or a high-confidence single-window signal for automated rollback/traffic-shift gating. We also add a confidence check that ensures at least N independent hosts observe the regression before initiating an automated rollback.

Risk and rollback: The change is behind a feature flag (perf.canary.adaptive_hysteresis) and defaults to off for existing customers. Rollout plan: enable for internal canaries, monitor canary.hysteresis_state and canary.alert_rate for 48h, then progressively enable for non-critical routes.

Notes: this PR focuses on detection/gating; follow-ups will expose UI controls in the Console and add a safety net around multi-model rollouts.

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Overall this looks strong. Two asks: (1) add a unit test for the adaptive threshold decay; (2) metric names should include `_v2` until we migrate dashboards.
Author (Asha): Added decay unit test and prefixed metrics with `_v2`. See latest commits. Added notes to migration section in docs.
Maya Chen: Can we formalize the host-count confidence check? Edge-case: autoscaled pools may report sparse data during cold-starts. Suggest requiring min_samples_per_host and min_hosts thresholds.
Author (Asha): Implemented min_samples_per_host and min_hosts parameters with sane defaults (3 samples, 2 hosts) and added test for cold-start behavior.
Liam O'Connor: CI perf-suite flagged a flaky integration test initially — looks fixed after host-cohort stability check. Approving once CI is green.
Diego Marquez: Approved after verifying metrics and test coverage. Left a small nit on logging verbosity.
